translations.text: A German prayer produced from the prayer above. Lord almighty, you who are the only comfort and the eternal salvation of all those who believe in you and hope in you,
enlighten my heart, so that I may reflect on your goodness and your grace, and on my sins and my wrongdoings, and may lament them before you as I need to.
Extinguish, Lord, everything in me that the hateful enemy kindles within me that is vain and unrighteous or impure,
and kindle in me the desire for eternal life, so that I may love it as I should and hunger and thirst after it as I need to.

Then make me so glad and so strong in all your service that I may endure all the hardships I must endure in this world for your honour and for your name, and for my own need or for anyone else's need.
Lord, give me the strength and also the skill for it. Then give me such faith and such hope in your goodness as I need, and such love,
such fear, humility and obedience, and such patience, as I ought to show to you, the Almighty, and to all the people I live among.
Then I pray that you give me such purity in my thoughts and in my body, sleeping or waking, that I may go worthily and acceptably to your altar and to all your service.
Then I pray that you grant me a share of all the virtues without which neither I nor anyone else can please you: first through your holy birth, through your passion and through the holy cross,
on which you redeemed the whole world, and through your resurrection and your ascension, and through the grace and comfort of the Holy Spirit.
With that comfort, comfort me and strengthen me against all dangers and against all the temptations of the hateful enemy.
Then help me through the prayers of Saint Mary, ever virgin, through the prayers of Saint Michael and the whole heavenly host, and through the prayers of Saint John the Baptist and Saint Peter,
Paul, Andrew, James, John and all your apostles, and through the prayers of all the children who were slain for your sake by Herod.
Then help me through the prayers of Saint Stephen, Saint Lawrence, Vitus, Pancras, George, Maurice, Denis, Gereon, Kilian, Boniface, Januarius, Hippolytus, Cyriacus, Sixtus and all their companions.
Then help me through the prayers of Saint Emmeram, Sebastian, Fabian, Quirinus, Vincent, Castulus, Blaise, Alban and Antoninus.
Then help me through the prayers of Saint Sylvester, Martin, Remigius, Gregory, Nicholas, Benedict, Basil, Patrick, Anthony, Hilarion, Ambrose, Augustine,
Jerome, Wolfgang, Zeno, Simeon, Bardo, Ulrich and Pope Leo, and through the prayers of the holy virgins Petronilla, Cecilia, Scholastica and Margaret.
Then help me through the prayers of all your saints, so that none of my sins and no snare of the hateful enemy may lead me so far astray that your grace abandons me.
Then I call upon your grace on behalf of our monastery, which has been destroyed because of our sins,
that it may be set right through your grace and through the intercessions of all your saints, for our needs and for all the needs of those who serve here or who seek grace here.
Remember, Lord, all of us through your manifold grace, and be mindful of this place, so that your honor and your praise may be here.
Remember also, Lord, all the congregations that are gathered anywhere in your name, and be mindful of them in all their needs.
After that I pray for all those who have commended themselves to my prayers by confession or by entreaty, whoever they may be,
wherever they may be, that you let them enjoy the hope that they have in your grace and also in my prayer.
Have mercy on them, Lord, and remember that you commanded us to pray for one another.
After that I call on your grace for all our rulers, clergy and laity alike, that you make them such that they can govern themselves rightly, and all who are subject and entrusted to them.
After that I pray for all my kinsfolk, that you be mindful of them according to your grace.
After that I pray for all those who ever did me any kindness or ever had any trouble on my account, from the beginning of my life until this hour, that you reward them where they most need it.
I pray also for all those who in any way were made worse by me or were left uncomforted, that you set them right and comfort them with your goodness.
After that I pray concerning all the injustice and all the strife and the bad weather that there is anywhere, that you, who can do all things, may look upon it all according to your grace.
After that I call out for all our departed brothers who are buried here, and for all those who are buried here, having departed in the true faith.
After that I pray for all the dead who have confraternity here, and for all those from whom we have ever received alms.
After that I pray for all those for whom anyone ought to pray for your grace, that they may benefit from all my life and from the fact that I am here surviving after them.
Lastly I commend myself and all my labors and all my diligence into your grace, so that,
where I myself cannot, or do not know how, or do not wish to take care of myself, through my frailty and through my carelessness or through my foolishness,
you may take care of me as you are able and know how, and as befits your goodness and your wisdom. Into your hands, Lord, I commend my spirit and my body.
O only hope, O eternal salvation and refuge of all who hope in you, God, have mercy on me, a wretch and a sinner, who seeks the protection of your grace.
Help me, Lord, and attend to my prayers, which I now desire to bring before you, not out of any confidence in my merits, but trusting only in the immensity of your mercy.

Enlighten first of all my heart, I beg, so that, considering in some measure the abundance of your goodness and of my wickedness, (51b) I may be able always to lament and to amend, with the worthy grief of penance, the things I have committed against you until now.
Next I pray, Lord, that whatever impurity, whatever vanity or error the most wicked enemy strives to kindle in me,

[…] that you may extinguish, and always kindle me to the fervour of your love and affection, and send into my heart that hunger and thirst by which I may burn with desire for the keeping of your commandments and for the joys of eternal life.

For although, through the gifts of your grace, I know that the joys of eternal life are to be preferred to all the pleasure of the present life, and although I have also been taught in various ways to desire and seek after these things,
yet no such knowledge benefits me unless, by the added help of your inspiration, you continually draw me there and grant me the desire, and also the opportunity and the strength, to do good.
For, alas, weakness and sloth can easily hold me back, frail and negligent as I am, from the whole purpose of the religious life.

Therefore, most merciful God, seeing this weakness in me, make me so sound and strong in the vigour of both the outer and the inner man that I may be joyful and ready in every effort of your service, and that all the labour
which I must continually carry out in this world, for reverence of your praise, for penance for my sins, and also for the needs of others, I may be able to bear.

I know, indeed, that you have many soldiers of such great virtue and such great devotion that, although they are afflicted with very many weaknesses and hardships, they are nevertheless found most ready and most steadfast in your commandments.
These, Lord, are made perfect by the gift of your grace and are chosen for the arms of your power.
But I, weighed down by every kind of frailty and sloth, as my sins deserve, can scarcely persevere in even a little effort of your service, even when I have full health and prosperity.
Therefore I beg you, most merciful God, not to let me be burdened by the trouble of sickness or adversity more than you know to be fitting for my condition.
Bear with me, I pray, faint-hearted and slothful as I am; wait for me, frail and weak as I am, until I turn to you at least a little.
Strengthen me, then, with such faith and hope that, being most certain of your promises, I may not fall into the dangers of any distrust or harmful sadness.

In addition, I pray, grant me such love and fear, and humility, and also patience and obedience, as I ought to show first to you, almighty God, and then to all people among whom it may ever fall to me to live.

Take from me, Lord, both ambition and delight in all worldly glory, and give me some share of spiritual wisdom, that it may be with me and labour with me, so that I may know what is acceptable before you (52b) at all times.
Do not remember, I beg you, the sins of my youth and of my ignorance, but according to your mercy remember me.
Grant me also, I beg you, purity of mind and body, waking or sleeping, so that I may approach the office of the altar and of all your service more worthily and carry it out acceptably.
Then I pray, Lord, that I may deserve to share in all the virtues without which no one can please you.
But since I cannot obtain such great gifts of your goodness by any efforts of my own, by your most holy nativity and passion, Lord Jesus Christ,
and also by the venerable cross on which you deigned to hang for the salvation of the world, and by your resurrection and ascension, and also by the grace of the Holy Spirit, grant me this, I pray.

Help me also through the merits and prayers of your most holy mother and ever-virgin Mary, and also through Saint Michael and all the heavenly powers, and through Saint John the Baptist, and through your holy apostles Peter and Paul,
Andrew, James and John, and through the intercessions of all your apostles, and also through the patronage of those most holy infants who were slaughtered by Herod for your name.
Come to my aid also through the prayers of your holy martyrs Stephen and Lawrence, Vitus and Pancras, George and Emmeram, Quirinus and Castulus,
Sebastian and Vincent, and also through Maurice and Denis, Gereon and Kilian, Boniface and Januarius, Sixtus and (53a) Cyriacus,
together with the patronage of their companions, and also through the prayers of your holy confessors Sylvester and Martin, Remigius and Gregory, Nicholas and Benedict, Ulrich and Wolfgang,
and through the holy virgins Petronilla and Cecilia, Scholastica and Margaret, and also through those saints whose relics are kept in this monastery or in this city,

and then through the intercessions of all your saints, help me, I beg, so that I may not, because of any of my sins, be handed over into the hands of those who pursue my soul, but may be defended always and everywhere by your accustomed mercy.

Next, Lord Jesus Christ, I humbly beg your boundless mercy for the site of our monastery: since, as our sins deserved, it has, alas, been destroyed inside and out, as much by our own people as by outsiders,

may it be restored through your grace and through the intercession of all your saints, to the praise of your name and for the use and needs of ourselves and of those who constantly serve us and of those who come here to obtain some favor.

To this I add a prayer for all who, gathered in your name, live anywhere in the holy Church: that they may follow with fitting conduct the rule of spiritual life that they profess by their habit, and that they may be worthy to receive from you the support of bodily life, as they need it.
Give them, I beg, eternal Shepherd, such shepherds and rulers as will guide them by their example not to perdition but to eternal salvation.

For those also who have taken care to commend themselves to the prayer of me, a sinner, by confession or by some other (53b) intercession, I humbly entreat your goodness, Lord, that the forgiveness they hoped for from their confession may not be made void because of any of my sins.

Remember, I pray, your mercy toward us, and the words of your apostle James, who says, "Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be saved," and grant that both their confession and my prayer, which I offer for them, may benefit them.

I pray also for the pope and the emperor or our king, and also for all our rulers and princes, that you may make them so perfect in love and fear of you that they may be able to govern themselves and those subject to them, and to lead them by fitting example.

In addition to these things, I also pray for my parents and relatives, and for those who, from the beginning of my life until this hour, have borne any kind of labour for my sake, and who have tried to help me in food or drink, in clothing or in teaching, or in any other way.

For all of these, then, I ask your mercy alone, Lord: since I cannot pay them any of the reward that I owe them, may you be pleased to repay them wherever there is need, whether in the present age or in the age to come.
I also pray for those whom I have ever saddened without cause, or led astray by any of my actions, that through the working of your goodness they may in some way be comforted and set right.
Then I pray to your majesty, Lord, for all Christian people together, that you may be pleased to grant them (54a) peace, mild weather and plenty of crops, according to their needs.
And although, surrounded by the snares of the devil or by human weakness, they turn away in various ways from the practice of the Christian faith, I still ask

that the knowledge of your holy name and the confession of your great majesty, to which they entrust themselves with fitting faith and in which they place their greatest hope of life, may benefit them for ever.

In addition to these things, Lord, I ask your boundless mercy for all our departed brothers, and for those for whom I have ever become bound to pray, whether through the fellowship of our brotherhood, through any request to be remembered, or through their generous almsgiving.
Then I pray for all who have died in the holy faith, that you may be pleased to free them from the places of punishment and to set them in everlasting rest.
So, Lord, graciously receive these prayers that I, a sinner, have brought before you for the living and for the dead alike, and grant that they may be of some benefit both to them and to me.

Finally, I know that none of the words of my prayer have been enough for me. Instead, I place in you the sufficiency and completion of all my actions, and into your hands, Lord, I commend my spirit and my body, together with every effort and concern

that any matter forces me to take on. Wherever I cannot, or do not know how to, or even do not want to guard myself, may you be pleased to keep me safe everywhere, as you are able and as you know how, and as you will according to your goodness.
